topic: Code-First AI Evals Guide 2026: Test Agents Like Software, Not Prompts

competitors.title: Braintrust: Evaluate systematically — AI evaluation guide
key_points: Full evaluation cycle: iterate in playgrounds → promote to experiments → automate in CI/CD → score in production → feed back into datasets
Three-part anatomy: Data (test cases), Task (function being evaluated), Scorers/Classifiers (quality measurement)
Offline evaluation runs against known datasets before deployment; online scoring evaluates production traces asynchronously
Supports code-based scorers, LLM-as-a-judge, and custom code scorers with span or trace scope
Best practices: start with 5-10 representative examples, validate scoring system, run evaluations in a loop, change one variable at a time

competitors.title: Braintrust: Evaluation best practices
key_points: Start with a small dataset (5-10 examples) covering core use cases — small well-chosen dataset beats large easy-case dataset
Validate scorers: test obvious cases, read LLM-as-judge reasoning, watch for bias (longer/formal outputs favored)
Run evaluations in a continuous loop: online scoring → surface failures → add to datasets → offline experiments → deploy → monitor
Change one variable at a time between experiments for interpretable results
Account for nondeterminism: use larger datasets or increase trial count rather than re-running experiments
Keep baselines current — stale baselines are the most common source of misleading eval results
Aggregate scores hide problems: use group-by with metadata to find regressions in specific categories

competitors.title: Galileo: Eval Engineering — the full lifecycle of AI evals
key_points: Eval Engineering is the merging of data science and software engineering: LLM features built as software, tested like ML systems
Six-step lifecycle: Creating LLM-as-Judge → Tuning the Eval → Developing with Evals → Fine-tuning the SLM → Deploying the Guardrail → Recycle Learnings
Untuned LLM-as-judge evals achieve only ~66-68% agreement with human SMEs at best
Tuning requires SME annotations, prompt optimization, and few-shot examples to reach >95% accuracy
Production-grade evals need SLM fine-tuning to bring latency below 150ms and observe 100% of traffic
Production evals at scale can cost up to $50K/day for millions of spans with LLM judges
Galileo's Luna-2 SLM family enables real-time scoring as production guardrails

competitors.title: Langfuse: Evaluation of LLM Applications
key_points: Evals run across the AI engineering loop: score live traces in production, turn examples into datasets, run experiments, judge with manual or automated evaluators
Online evaluation on live production traces; offline evaluation before shipping changes
Supports annotation queues, LLM-as-a-judge, code evaluators, and scores via API/SDK
CI/CD experiments block deploys on regressions
Score Analytics dashboard for trending evaluation scores over time across multiple evaluators
29K GitHub stars, 300+ contributors, trusted by 19 of Fortune 50 and 63 of Fortune 500

competitors.title: Braintrust: Evals Foundations — free evals course
key_points: 14-module course across three sections: Learn, Build, Refine — takes about an hour
Covers deterministic and LLM-as-judge scorers, comparing prompt variants, turning production traces into test cases
Used by teams at Ramp, Notion, and OpenAI to ship quality AI products
Teaches the eval improvement loop: trace everything, score online, analyze, iterate

angles: Why traditional software testing fundamentally breaks for multi-step agents — and how code-first evals fill the gap with deterministic checks, trajectory scoring, and LLM-as-judge
The eval engineering lifecycle: from creating an LLM-as-judge prompt to fine-tuning an SLM for sub-150ms production guardrails at 100% traffic coverage
Code-first vs prompt-first: writing evals as Python/TypeScript functions with version control, CI/CD gates, and reproducible experiments — not ad-hoc prompt tweaking
The three-part anatomy of every eval: Data (golden datasets), Task (the agent function), Scorers (deterministic, LLM-as-judge, or custom code) — and how to build each
Online vs offline evaluation: pre-deployment validation catches regressions before users see them; production monitoring surfaces edge cases you never anticipated
The eval improvement loop: score production traces → surface failures → add to datasets → run experiments → deploy → repeat — closing the gap between test and real-world
Tool selection framework: Braintrust for eval-first CI/CD workflows, Langfuse for production observability + evaluation, Galileo for full lifecycle from prompt tuning to SLM guardrails
The silent killer: tool-call errors that cascade downstream — how code-first evals detect them at step 2, not at the final output
